papers.title: Uninflamed colonic tissue harbors humoral activity linked to anti-TNF therapy non-response in ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: Anti-TNF therapy is central for treating ulcerative colitis, yet ∼40% are primary non-responders. To find pre-treatment signatures distinguishing anti-TNF non-responders from responders, we did serum cytokine profiling and laser microdissection transcriptomics on paired uninflamed and inflamed colonic epithelium and lamina propria from patients matched at baseline but differing in endoscopic outcome. Although inflammation drove more epithelial changes, the signatures separating non-responders from responders were found in uninflamed lamina propria, with elevated cell-cycle genes and a co-expre
papers.summary: This study identifies pre-treatment molecular signatures that distinguish ulcerative colitis patients who will not respond to anti-TNF therapy from those who will. Using serum cytokine profiling and laser microdissection transcriptomics on paired inflamed and uninflamed colonic tissue, the authors found that non-responder signatures localize to uninflamed lamina propria, characterized by elevated cell-cycle gene expression and a co-expression module linked to humoral activity. These findings suggest that baseline immune activity in non-inflamed tissue, rather than inflammation itself, may drive primary anti-TNF non-response.

papers.title: A Molecularly Anchored Spatial Transcriptomic Framework for Precise CA1-Subiculum Parcellation and Region-Resolved Analysis in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: The precise molecular delineation of the interface between the Subiculum (Sub) and cornu ammonis 1 (CA1) is a challenge in hippocampal research, as conventional cytoarchitectural boundaries are often ambiguous and limit reproducible regional annotation. Here, we developed a molecularly anchored spatial transcriptomic framework to define CA1-Sub regional identities using high-definition spatial transcriptomics (Stereo-seq) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) references.
papers.summary: This study presents a spatial transcriptomics framework that uses Stereo-seq and single-nucleus RNA-seq to molecularly define the boundary between the CA1 and Subiculum regions of the hippocampus, addressing the ambiguity of traditional cytoarchitectural boundaries. The approach enables more precise and reproducible regional annotation, which the authors apply to region-resolved analysis in Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics in adult Drosophila neurons.
papers.abstract: The Drosophila adult central brain contains 240 circadian neurons, of which there are more than 25 different neuron subtypes based on connectomic data. Recent single-cell RNA-seq characterization of these neurons "around the clock" also indicates a similar number of molecular subtypes of circadian neurons, but other conclusions from these transcriptomic studies warranted verifying and extending with other approaches. To address these limitations, we used three complementary approaches: 1) We used a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons from multiple t
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study uses a genetic multiplexing strategy combined with single-cell transcriptomics to profile circadian neurons in the adult Drosophila brain across the day-night cycle. It reveals cell-type-specific transcriptional dynamics in response to circadian rhythms and light, providing a higher-resolution view of how distinct neuron subtypes regulate daily gene expression.

papers.title: Multi-omics and experimental validation identify RAPGEF2 as a protective prognostic biomarker in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Kidney Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma (KIRC) is characterized by marked molecular heterogeneity and metabolic reprogramming, underscoring the need for reliable biomarkers for prognostic assessment and individualized treatment. RAPGEF2, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor has been implicated in cell adhesion and differentiation, but its role in KIRC remains unclear. In this study, we systematically evaluated the expression pattern, prognostic significance, genomic associations, biological function, and therapeutic relevance of RAPGEF2 in KIRC through integrated multi-omics analyses and experimenta
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with experimental validation to show that RAPGEF2, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor, is downregulated in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and is associated with better patient prognosis. The authors characterize its expression, genomic associations, and biological functions, proposing RAPGEF2 as a protective prognostic biomarker for this cancer.

papers.title: TRPV1-STAT3 signaling as a driver of lethal pathology during pneumococcal nose-to-brain invasion.
papers.abstract: Nose-to-brain infection represents a non-hematogenous route by which pathogens invade the central nervous system via neural pathways. The olfactory and trigeminal systems are implicated in this process, but the molecular mechanisms underlying lethal pathology remain incompletely understood. We hypothesized that trigeminal TRPV1 and downstream STAT3 signaling contribute to disease progression during pneumococcal nose-to-brain infection. A murine intranasal infection model using Streptococcus pneumoniae was established with methimazole-induced olfactory epithelial damage and/or resiniferatoxin-m
papers.summary: This study uses a mouse model of intranasal Streptococcus pneumoniae infection to show that signaling through the TRPV1 receptor and downstream STAT3 pathway in the trigeminal system drives lethal pathology during nose-to-brain invasion. Blocking or genetically disrupting this pathway reduced disease severity, suggesting a targetable mechanism for bacterial meningitis.

papers.title: Multi-modal analysis of vascular remodelling in human obliterative bronchiolitis after lung transplantation.
papers.abstract: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) is the leading cause of late morbidity and mortality after lung transplantation. Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS), a major CLAD phenotype, is characterized by obliterative bronchiolitis (OB). While microvascular perturbations are described in BOS, their cellular and molecular characteristics remain unclear. Intact human CLAD lungs (n=3) underwent hierarchical phase-contrast tomography (HiP-CT) for three-dimensional vascular mapping. In OB-affected airways vs. controls (n=4 each), endothelial subtypes were characterized by multiplex immunofluores
papers.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
papers.summary: This study uses hierarchical phase-contrast tomography (HiP-CT) and multiplex immunofluorescence to map vascular remodeling in human lungs with obliterative bronchiolitis (OB) after lung transplantation. It identifies distinct endothelial subtypes and microvascular perturbations in OB-affected airways compared to controls, providing new cellular and molecular insights into chronic lung allograft dysfunction.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals atorvastatin modulates the tumor microenvironment to suppress breast cancer liver metastatic outgrowth.
papers.abstract: Metastatic breast cancer remains incurable, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic strategies. Epidemiological and preclinical evidence suggests statins suppress metastatic outgrowth, however the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We employed high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (ST) to explore the cellular composition and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the metastatic microenvironment following atorvastatin treatment. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded breast cancer liver metastases from control and atorvastatin-treated mice were analyzed by Nanostring CosMx Spatial Molecul
papers.summary: Using high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (Nanostring CosMx) on breast cancer liver metastases in mice, this study shows that atorvastatin alters the metastatic tumor microenvironment and gene expression to suppress metastatic outgrowth. The work links a commonly used statin to specific cellular and transcriptional changes in the liver metastatic niche, offering mechanistic insight into how statins may limit breast cancer progression.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological factors (covariates) from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing the problem of multicollinearity in human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, and enables counterfactual 'what-if' analyses of epigenomic variation.

papers.title: OscillomeR infers ultradian oscillations and targets of the Hes family.
papers.abstract: The Hes family, basic-helix-loop-helix transcription factors and downstream effectors of Notch signaling, regulate the fate choices of pancreatic progenitors, muscle stem cells, neuronal progenitors, and presomitic mesoderm cells. Bioluminescence imaging (BLI) has revealed ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family members Hes1, Hes5, and Hes7. However, identifying which of the Hes target genes also oscillate remains challenging due to the time-consuming and costly nature of tracking individual target genes using BLI. Here, we propose OscillomeR, a computational framework that reconstructs u
papers.summary: OscillomeR is a computational framework that infers ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family transcription factors and predicts which of their downstream target genes also oscillate. It addresses the difficulty of experimentally tracking individual targets via bioluminescence imaging by using computational reconstruction instead. This could help uncover oscillatory gene networks in developmental contexts like pancreatic, muscle, and neuronal progenitors.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: This paper introduces a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, using a gradient-boosted meta-classifier trained on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (e.g., GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, ARACNe) to resolve disagreements between methods on a per-edge basis rather than choosing one method or averaging all. The authors also present a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts, evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens.

papers.title: FAP+ pericyte-like cells promote monocyte differentiation into tumor-associated macrophages in glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive primary brain tumor characterized by profound immunosuppression that facilitates tumor progression and promotes therapeutic resistance. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a recognized theranostic target in multiple cancers, is upregulated in GBM and predominantly expressed by pericyte-like stromal cells. Here we identify a role for FAP⁺ pericyte-like cells in shaping the GBM immune microenvironment through monocyte recruitment and differentiation. Analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) datasets, supported by reverse-transcription quantitative PCR
papers.summary: This study shows that FAP-expressing pericyte-like stromal cells in glioblastoma recruit monocytes and drive their differentiation into tumor-associated macrophages, contributing to the immunosuppressive microenvironment. The findings highlight FAP+ pericytes as a potential therapeutic target for disrupting this pro-tumor immune crosstalk.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveal impaired metabolic liver zonation in acute-on-chronic liver failure.
papers.abstract: Extrahepatic organ failures are key determinants of acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF). While the role of systemic inflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathogenesis of ACLF is well known, the contribution of the liver itself is less understood. We therefore performed transcriptome and functional analyses of the liver in order to identify hepatic drivers of ACLF.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to map gene expression across liver regions in acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), revealing that the liver's normal metabolic zonation—the spatial division of metabolic functions across lobules—becomes impaired. The findings suggest that disrupted hepatic metabolic organization, not just systemic inflammation, contributes to the organ failures seen in ACLF.

papers.title: Polyethylene terephthalate micro-/nanoplastics suppress SAT1-dependent ferroptosis in triple-negative breast cancer.
papers.abstract: The potential association between micro-/nanoplastics and cancer has raised increasing concerns. However, research focusing specifically on breast cancer (BC), and particularly on triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), remains limited, leading to a critical gap in current knowledge. This study seeks to explore potential correlative effects of micro-/nanoplastic exposure on TNBC progression.
papers.summary: This study investigates how exposure to polyethylene terephthalate (PET) micro-/nanoplastics affects triple-negative breast cancer progression. The authors find that these plastic particles suppress SAT1-dependent ferroptosis, a form of iron-dependent cell death, potentially promoting tumor survival. This suggests a novel mechanism linking environmental plastic pollution to cancer aggressiveness.

papers.title: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Data to Identify Lactylation-Related Gene Signatures in Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Using Machine Learning Algorithms.
papers.abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI) is not only a common complication of liver transplantation and major hepatic surgery but also a critical determinant of postoperative prognosis. Lactate metabolic reprogramming has been observed in HIRI, yet the role of lactate and its related lactylation in the pathogenesis of HIRI remains unclear. To address this, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data with multiple bioinformatic approaches. Five single-cell gene set activity scoring methods (AUCell, UCell, singscore, ssGSEA, and AddModuleScore) were applied to evaluate lactylation activity
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data to investigate lactylation-related gene signatures in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI), a common complication of liver transplantation and surgery. Using five gene set activity scoring methods and machine learning algorithms, the authors identify lactylation-associated gene signatures that may contribute to HIRI pathogenesis. The work highlights lactate metabolic reprogramming and protein lactylation as potentially important mechanisms in HIRI.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from NSCLC patients to build a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) based on epithelial cell-derived genes, using machine learning to predict immunotherapy response and survival. The signature stratifies patients into high- and low-PIS groups with distinct immune profiles, and the authors validate ADAM12 as a key functional regulator through cell line assays and mouse models. The work suggests PIS could serve as a biomarker for guiding immunotherapy decisions in NSCLC.

papers.title: NEAT1 Coordinates a PDLIM5-CACNA1C Regulatory Program Associated with a Potentially Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyocyte State in the Border Zone During Early Myocardial Infarction.
papers.abstract: Patients with early-stage myocardial infarction (MI) are at high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias, yet the cell-type-specific molecular landscape associated with post-infarction arrhythmogenesis has not been systematically characterized. This study integrates single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics to define a cardiomyocyte subpopulation in early MI and dissect the NEAT1-centered regulatory network driving its ion channel remodeling. Single-nucleus transcriptomic data from post-MI human hearts were re-analyzed to identify a distinct subpopulation, termed arrhythmia-potential cardio
papers.summary: This study integrates single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics to identify a distinct cardiomyocyte subpopulation in the border zone of early myocardial infarction that may be prone to arrhythmias. The authors show that the long non-coding RNA NEAT1 coordinates a regulatory program involving PDLIM5 and CACNA1C, driving ion channel remodeling in this cell state. The findings suggest a cell-type-specific molecular mechanism linking early post-MI transcriptional changes to malignant ventricular arrhythmia risk.

papers.title: Deciphering the Genetic Underpinnings of Liver Cirrhosis-Heart Failure Comorbidity Through Multi-Omics: CRIM1 as a Key Endothelial Mediator.
papers.abstract: The co-occurrence of liver cirrhosis (LC) and heart failure (HF) poses considerable clinical challenges, yet the cellular and molecular determinants of this comorbidity remain poorly characterized. To address this, we developed an integrative multi-omics pipeline encompassing GWAS meta-analysis, gsMap-based spatial transcriptomic projection, GeneEnrich functional annotation, single-cell atlas construction, seismicGWAS and ECLIPSER cell-type scoring, eCAVIAR and fastenloc colocalization, hdWGCNA network inference, scTenifoldKnk in silico gene perturbation, and GCTA-COJO fine-mapping. Quality-co
papers.summary: This study integrates GWAS meta-analysis with spatial transcriptomics, single-cell atlases, and multiple colocalization and network-inference tools to identify genetic and cellular drivers of the comorbidity between liver cirrhosis and heart failure. The authors pinpoint CRIM1 as a key endothelial mediator linking the two diseases, highlighting shared vascular/endothelial mechanisms. The work demonstrates a multi-omics framework for dissecting complex disease comorbidities.

papers.title: Machine learning identifies ac4C-related prognostic signature and TUBA1C as therapeutic target in COAD.
papers.abstract: To explore the role of N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes (acRGs) in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and identify reliable prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. Multi-source transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-COAD, GSE39582, GSE17536) and single-cell RNA-seq data were analyzed. Ten machine learning algorithms were integrated to construct an acRG-based prognostic signature (acRGBS). Immune microenvironment (TME) and genomic profiling were performed, with in vitro functional experiments validating TUBA1C's role. acRGBS, comprising four hub genes (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C), e
papers.journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
papers.summary: This study used multi-source transcriptomic datasets and ten integrated machine learning algorithms to build an ac4C-related gene prognostic signature (acRGBS) for colon adenocarcinoma, identifying four hub genes including TUBA1C. The signature was linked to immune microenvironment and genomic features, and in vitro experiments validated TUBA1C as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: A High-Resolution Stereo-Seq Spatial Transcriptomic Resource for Adult Holstein Cattle Liver.
papers.abstract: The bovine liver is a highly compartmentalized organ that plays essential roles in continuous gluconeogenesis and nitrogen recycling; however, its spatial molecular architecture has remained largely uncharacterized due to the limitations of traditional bulk and single-cell approaches. To address this gap, Spatial Enhanced Resolution Omics-sequencing (Stereo-seq) was utilized to generate a subcellular-resolution (500 nm) transcriptomic map of an adult Holstein cattle liver, and a refined reference-guided workflow was implemented to overcome standard annotation limitations in livestock. Raw sequ
papers.summary: This study generated a subcellular-resolution (500 nm) spatial transcriptomic map of an adult Holstein cattle liver using Stereo-seq, providing the first detailed spatial molecular atlas of the bovine liver. The authors also developed a refined reference-guided workflow to overcome annotation challenges in livestock species, enabling identification of spatially organized functional zones involved in gluconeogenesis and nitrogen recycling.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning to identify a gene signature linked to tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The authors show that this TDT-related signature has prognostic value and highlights potential therapeutic targets, while accounting for HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This study benchmarks computational tools for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data generated with Nanopore long-read sequencing, using paired short-read and long-read datasets. The authors systematically compare methods for tasks like isoform detection and alternative splicing analysis, providing guidance on tool performance and trade-offs. It serves as a practical resource for researchers choosing bioinformatics pipelines for long-read single-cell transcriptomics.

papers.title: Interpretable multi-omics integration across mixed-order tensors with MANTRA.
papers.abstract: The integration of multi-modal molecular data is crucial for understanding complex diseases, but existing methods struggle with modern experimental designs that generate datasets with mixed-order tensors-for example, a third-order drug-response tensor alongside a second-order transcriptomics matrix. Here, we present MANTRA (Multi-view ANalysis with Tensor and matRix Alignment), a probabilistic framework that integrates collections of tensors of different orders, combining the strengths of group factor analysis and tensor decomposition. MANTRA learns interpretable latent factors and naturally h
papers.summary: MANTRA is a probabilistic framework that integrates multi-omics datasets with mixed-order tensors, such as combining a third-order drug-response tensor with a second-order transcriptomics matrix. It extends group factor analysis and tensor decomposition to learn interpretable latent factors across heterogeneous data structures. This addresses a key gap in multi-modal integration for complex disease studies.

papers.title: Alignment-free integration of single-nucleus ATAC-seq across species with sPYce.
papers.abstract: Changes in gene regulation largely contribute to differences in cellular identities and phenotypes between species. Single-nucleus assays for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing (snATAC-seq) are an efficient strategy to identify putative gene regulatory elements and provide new insight into evolutionary divergence of regulatory programmes. However, no dedicated framework exists to integrate and compare snATAC-seq data across species, while methods designed for single-cell gene expression data have serious limitations. Here we present sPYce, a cross-species snATAC-seq integration m
papers.summary: The authors present sPYce, a new computational framework for integrating single-nucleus ATAC-seq data across species without relying on sequence alignment. This addresses a gap where existing single-cell integration methods, designed for gene expression data, perform poorly on chromatin accessibility data. sPYce enables direct comparison of regulatory programs between species, offering new insights into the evolution of gene regulation.

papers.title: Ten quick tips for spatial transcriptomics analysis.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while retaining spatial context within tissue sections. Since the foundational work by Ståhl et al. in 2016, the field has expanded rapidly, with diverse platforms now spanning sequencing-based (e.g., Visium, Visium HD, Slide-seq, Stereo-seq, and Seq-Scope) and imaging-based (e.g., MERFISH, Xenium, and CosMx SMI) approaches. The breadth of platforms, data structures, and computational tools, however, can be daunting for newcomers. Here, we present ten quick tips spanning the entire ST research workflow: whether ST suits
papers.summary: This paper provides ten practical tips for researchers new to spatial transcriptomics, covering the full workflow from experimental design through computational analysis. It addresses the rapidly expanding landscape of sequencing-based and imaging-based platforms, helping newcomers navigate platform choices, data structures, and analysis tools.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics and Radiogenomic Analysis Identifies S100B and ITGB5 as Complementary Candidate Biomarkers of Glioblastoma Heterogeneity.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity, diffuse invasion, and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In this study, we applied an integrative multi-omics and radiogenomic framework to identify candidate biomarkers reflecting complementary dimensions of GBM heterogeneity. Public bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated to define GBM-related differentially expressed genes, which were intersected with curated microbiota-associated gene sets as a hypothesis-generating screening strategy. Machine-learning models with SHAP interpretation were use
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomic data, microbiota-associated gene sets, and radiogenomic features to identify candidate biomarkers of glioblastoma heterogeneity. Using machine-learning models with SHAP interpretation, the authors nominate S100B and ITGB5 as complementary biomarkers capturing distinct dimensions of tumor heterogeneity. The work is hypothesis-generating and requires experimental validation.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Multimodal Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Senescence-Related Prognostic Signature and Characterizes ADGRF5-Associated Malignant Phenotypes in Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence (CS) is increasingly recognized as an important cell-state programme involved in breast cancer progression and therapeutic response, but its context-dependent molecular heterogeneity limits its application in prognostic assessment. In this study, GeneCompass-based all-gene in silico perturbation analysis was performed to identify candidate genes predicted to induce senescence or rejuvenation, thereby expanding the known senescence-related gene set. Machine learning further established a seven-gene prognostic signature that may serve as an adjunctive tool for prognostic asse
papers.summary: This study uses an AI model (GeneCompass) to computationally perturb genes and predict which ones drive senescence or rejuvenation in breast cancer, expanding the known senescence-related gene set. A machine-learning-derived seven-gene signature was then built as a prognostic tool, and ADGRF5 was linked to malignant phenotypes.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing data with machine learning to dissect the ovarian cancer microenvironment, focusing on how chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets drive poor outcomes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The authors identify fibroblast-enriched residual disease as a key contributor to adverse prognosis, highlighting candidate cell populations and inflammatory programs as potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Combined multi-omics profiling and machine learning analysis reveals that Bregs and RPS2 promote bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The bone is the primary site of distant metastasis in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), and bone metastasis (BM) significantly increases mortality. Deciphering the complex crosstalk between cancer cells and their tumor microenvironment (TME) is crucial for identifying therapeutic targets aimed at eliminating metastasis-initiating cells and preventing the establishment of overt metastases. Regulatory B cells (Bregs), a specialized B-cell subset endowed with potent immunosuppressive functions, play a pivotal regulatory role within the TME. However, their specific contributions, pheno
papers.summary: This study combines multi-omics profiling with machine learning to investigate how regulatory B cells (Bregs) and the gene RPS2 contribute to bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The authors identify Bregs and RPS2 as potential drivers of the metastatic process, suggesting them as candidate therapeutic targets. The work highlights the importance of cancer-immune crosstalk in the tumor microenvironment for bone metastasis.

papers.title: STC1 is associated with tumor progression and suppressive niches in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) exhibits high recurrence and therapy resistance. We aimed to investigate the undefined role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in LSCC pathogenesis.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC), a cancer with high recurrence and therapy resistance. The authors associate STC1 expression with tumor progression and immunosuppressive niches, suggesting it may contribute to LSCC pathogenesis. The findings point to STC1 as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target, though the abstract provides limited mechanistic detail.

papers.title: Microplastics and nanoplastics-related genes signature predicts prognosis in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and functional validation of interleukin 1 alpha.
papers.abstract: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs), as emerging environmental pollutants, have garnered significant attention from the global scientific community due to their potential threats to human health, particularly their association with the occurrence and development of cancer. The goal of our study is to create a predictive marker for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PAAD) based on MNPs-related genes, with the purposes of predicting survival outcomes and assessing the tumor immune microenvironment.
papers.summary: This study developed a gene expression signature based on microplastics- and nanoplastics-related genes to predict survival outcomes in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PAAD) and to characterize the tumor immune microenvironment. The authors also functionally validated interleukin 1 alpha (IL1A) as a key gene within this signature, linking environmental pollutant exposure to cancer prognosis.

papers.title: RECQL correlates with immune infiltration and serves as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic predictor in gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: RecQ-like helicase (RECQL), a member of the RecQ-like DNA helicase family, plays a crucial role in maintaining genomic stability. However, its relevance in gastric cancer (GC) has not been fully investigated. This study aimed to explore the clinical significance, biological functions, and potential role of RECQL in the tumor immune microenvironment of GC through comprehensive bioinformatics analyses and in vitro experiments.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of RECQL, a DNA helicase involved in genomic stability, in gastric cancer using bioinformatics and in vitro experiments. The authors report that RECQL expression correlates with immune cell infiltration and may serve as a prognostic biomarker and predictor of therapeutic response in gastric cancer patients.

papers.title: Multi-omics characterization of a GPRC5A+ epithelial subpopulation associated with malignant features in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) exhibits marked cellular heterogeneity, and the cellular context of malignancy-associated epithelial programs remains incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics profiling to identify and characterize a GPRC5A+ epithelial subpopulation in colorectal cancer that is associated with malignant features. The work links this specific cell population to tumor aggressiveness, providing a potential cellular context for malignancy-associated epithelial programs.

papers.title: Integration of Spatial Transcriptomics and Mendelian Randomization Identifies Candidate Molecular Regulators of Endometrial Cancer Progression.
papers.abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) is a common gynecologic malignancy arising from the epithelial cells of the endometrium. The marked cellular heterogeneity of EC and features of its tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) contribute to disease complexity and have been associated with poor prognosis. This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and Mendelian randomization (MR) to identify candidate genes associated with EC. Single-cell analysis identified MM0 as a putative stemness-associated transcriptional subpopulation with the highest CytoTRACE-inferred score; irGSEA indic
papers.summary: This study combines single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and Mendelian randomization to identify candidate genes driving endometrial cancer progression. The authors pinpoint a stemness-associated macrophage subpopulation (MM0) and use genetic causal inference to nominate molecular regulators within the tumor immune microenvironment. The work illustrates how integrating spatial and genetic epidemiology approaches can prioritize therapeutic targets in heterogeneous tumors.

papers.title: The Dual Face of Gingival Mesenchymal Stem Cell Paracrine Signalling in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Pro-Tumour Transcriptional Programme and a Hypothesis-Generating Drug-Repurposing Screen.
papers.abstract: Background: In our companion study, the gingival mesenchymal stem cell (GMSC) secretome suppresses oxidative stress and induces apoptosis in primary oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cells, where those wet-lab results are themselves reported as preliminary; here we ask whether it also engages a proliferation × migration programme in patient tissue. The two arms differ in read-out type (apoptosis and redox there, transcript abundance here), not in opposed function. Methods: Primary OSCC cells received GMSC-conditioned medium (GMSC-CM) or indirect Transwell co-culture, assayed by RT-qPCR (VEGF
papers.summary: This study examines how paracrine signals from gingival mesenchymal stem cells (GMSCs) affect oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cells, finding that GMSC-conditioned medium induces a pro-tumour transcriptional programme related to proliferation and migration in patient tissue. The authors also perform a hypothesis-generating drug-repurposing screen, highlighting the dual, context-dependent nature of GMSC paracrine signalling in OSCC.

papers.title: Particulate Matter Exposure and Diabetic Kidney Dysfunction: Insights from Integrated Transcriptomic and Bioinformatics Analyses.
papers.abstract: Exposure to ambient particulate matter (PM) has been linked to renal dysfunction, particularly in diabetic populations, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We performed bidirectional Mendelian randomization to assess causal relationships between PM exposure and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), integrated transcriptomic datasets to identify PM-related genes overlapping with diabetic kidney disease (DKD) differentially expressed genes, and applied machine learning approaches to select key feature genes and construct diagnostic models. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic
papers.summary: This study combines Mendelian randomization, transcriptomic integration, and machine learning to investigate how particulate matter exposure contributes to diabetic kidney dysfunction. The authors identify PM-related genes that overlap with diabetic kidney disease differentially expressed genes and build diagnostic models using key feature genes, with additional single-cell and spatial transcriptomic validation.

papers.title: STADiffuser: high-fidelity simulation and full-view 3D modeling of spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics technologies have provided invaluable insights by profiling gene expression alongside precise spatial information. However, they encounter high costs, data sparsity, and limited resolution, hindering their broader adoption and utility. Moreover, the lack of flexible simulators capable of generating high-fidelity simulated data has impeded the development of computational tools for spatial transcriptomic data analysis. To this end, we introduce STADiffuser, a versatile deep generative model that leverages diffusion modeling for accurate simulation of spatial transcriptom
papers.summary: STADiffuser is a deep generative diffusion model that simulates high-fidelity spatial transcriptomics data and enables full-view 3D modeling of tissue samples. It addresses key limitations of real spatial transcriptomics data—high cost, sparsity, and limited resolution—by providing a flexible simulator that can generate realistic data for benchmarking computational tools. The method also reconstructs complete 3D spatial expression landscapes from partial or low-resolution measurements.

papers.title: Pseudotime-conditioned diffusion models for imputing time-series single-cell data.
papers.abstract: Probabilistic diffusion-based imputation methods have demonstrated superior performance over many state-of-the-art approaches for imputing single-cell data. However, existing methods typically rely on isotropic Gaussian noise and canonical observation time, limiting their ability to capture structured temporal dependencies and continuous cellular dynamics. In time-series single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data, these limitations are exacerbated by the small number of experimentally measured time points and the substantial heterogeneity among cells collected at the same time point, causing observe
papers.summary: The authors propose a pseudotime-conditioned diffusion model for imputing time-series single-cell RNA-seq data. By conditioning on pseudotime rather than canonical observation times and using structured noise, the method better captures continuous cellular dynamics and temporal dependencies. This addresses limitations of existing diffusion-based imputation methods that struggle with sparse time points and cell heterogeneity.

papers.title: Multi-omics and machine learning reveal LYZ and ISG15 as diagnostic and therapeutic targets in autoimmune-mediated chronic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: CKD represents a substantial worldwide health challenge, defined by the gradual development of tubulointerstitial fibrosis and reduced renal performance. Autoimmune-mediated factors are central to this pathological process, yet early diagnostic biomarkers and specific therapeutic targets are scarce. The objective of this research is to systematically pinpoint crucial specific genes that contribute to autoimmune-mediated CKD progression.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with machine learning to identify LYZ and ISG15 as key genes involved in autoimmune-mediated chronic kidney disease. The authors propose these genes as potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets, addressing the scarcity of early markers for this condition.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of a Two-Gene NK Cell-Related Risk Model for COPD: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) involves chronic inflammation with potential involvement of natural killer (NK) cells, but NK cell-related diagnostic markers remain limited. This study aimed to identify NK cell-related hub genes and construct a risk model for COPD.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to identify NK cell-related hub genes and build a two-gene risk model for COPD. The model is validated as a potential diagnostic tool, highlighting NK cell involvement in COPD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Progress and challenges in exploring the pathogenesis of depressive disorders via RNA sequencing.
papers.abstract: Depressive disorders (DD) are highly heterogeneous psychiatric illnesses. Their complex pathogenesis, coupled with suboptimal response rates to current clinical treatments, poses significant challenges to global mental health. High-throughput RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool for dissecting the molecular mechanisms of DD at the transcriptomic level. This paper reviews recent advances utilizing bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq), and single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq) to explore the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), perinatal depression (PND), per
papers.summary: This review surveys how bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing have been applied to uncover transcriptomic mechanisms underlying depressive disorders, including major depressive disorder and perinatal depression. It highlights both the insights gained into disease heterogeneity and pathogenesis and the methodological and interpretive challenges that remain.

papers.title: Single-cell Raman profiling of B cell differentiation and leukemic transformation with transcriptome inference.
papers.abstract: Label-free profiling of cellular transcriptional and metabolic states during B cell differentiation and malignant transformation remains technically challenging. Raman spectroscopy offers a non-destructive alternative for single-cell biochemical characterization, yet its ability to infer transcriptomic profiles and distinguish leukemic cells has been limited.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell Raman spectroscopy to profile B cell differentiation and leukemic transformation, aiming to infer transcriptomic states from label-free biochemical signatures. The authors demonstrate that Raman profiling can distinguish leukemic cells from normal differentiating B cells, offering a non-destructive alternative to conventional transcriptomic methods.

papers.title: From transcriptomic profiling to precision oncology: a bibliometric analysis of RNA sequencing in acute myeloid leukemia.
papers.abstract: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has become an important tool for investigating the molecular heterogeneity of acute myeloid leukemia (AML); however, the global development and thematic evolution of this field remain inadequately characterized.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the global research landscape of RNA sequencing in acute myeloid leukemia, examining publication trends, key contributors, and thematic evolution over time. It characterizes how the field has moved from basic transcriptomic profiling toward precision oncology applications, though the abstract provides limited detail on specific findings.

papers.title: Peripheral blood cells and immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis: a retrospective clinical study with pharmacovigilance and single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis (ICI-M) is a rare but potentially lethal immune-related adverse event (irAE). Early identification of fulminant (severe) cases remains challenging, and the peripheral immune derangements underlying ICI-M are incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This retrospective clinical study investigates peripheral blood cell patterns in patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-M), a rare but potentially fatal side effect of cancer immunotherapy. By combining pharmacovigilance data with single-cell analysis, the authors aim to identify early markers of severe (fulminant) cases and characterize the immune cell changes in the blood that underlie this condition.

papers.title: An hiPSC-derived multi-lineage lung model exhibiting proximal-distal epithelial features for modeling pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and irreversible interstitial lung disease with limited therapeutic options. Existing hiPSC-derived lung organoid models are largely restricted to single epithelial lineages and cannot endogenously integrate multiple pulmonary cell types, limiting mechanistic studies and drug screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: The authors developed a human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived multi-lineage lung model that captures both proximal and distal epithelial features, overcoming the single-lineage limitation of prior lung organoid systems. This model enables endogenous integration of multiple pulmonary cell types and is applied to study pulmonary fibrosis, offering a more physiologically relevant platform for mechanistic research and drug screening in IPF.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk variants to a specific immune cell state—JAML+ lipid-associated macrophages—that shows high transcriptome-wide association activity. By combining single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niche mapping, and machine learning-based selection, the authors link genetic susceptibility to a pathogenic macrophage program in the diseased liver. The work provides a cell-type-specific framework for understanding how PSC risk genes drive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics and a boundary wound model reveal temporal decoupling and microenvironmental heterogeneity in radiation-induced fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy is a key treatment method for cancer, but high-dose treatment can lead to damage to normal tissues and chronic fibrosis. There is a lack of systematic temporal analysis of the dynamic progression from early damage signals to late extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics combined with a boundary wound model to track how radiation-induced fibrosis develops over time. The authors find that early damage signaling and later extracellular matrix deposition are temporally decoupled, and that the fibrotic microenvironment is heterogeneous across cell populations. This provides a more systematic temporal map of the progression from acute radiation damage to chronic fibrosis.

papers.title: Benchmarking computational decontamination of ambient RNA.
papers.abstract: Gene expression profiling of single cells using single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (sxRNA-seq) enables researchers to characterize cellular heterogeneity and unraveling complex biological processes at unprecedented resolution. However, sxRNA-seq faces challenges due to the presence of ambient RNA, extraneous RNA molecules not originating from the cells of interest. Sample preparation is a major source of ambient RNA, where harsh conditions can lead to cell lysis and the release of intracellular RNA. This inescapable inclusion of ambient RNA can cause erroneous results and hinder dow
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks computational methods for removing ambient RNA contamination from single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data. It evaluates how well different decontamination tools perform, highlighting that sample preparation (especially harsh conditions causing cell lysis) is a major source of this contaminating RNA. The study provides guidance on which computational approaches are most effective for cleaning up sxRNA-seq data.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification of MBNL2 associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) improves outcomes in resectable lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), yet response varies widely and current biomarkers lack precision. Novel correlates of immunotherapy sensitivity tailored to the LUSC tumor microenvironment (TME) are urgently needed.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics profiling to identify MBNL2 as a biomarker associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma. The finding suggests MBNL2 could help stratify patients likely to benefit from this treatment approach.

papers.title: Bulk and single cell RNA sequencing data reveal lactylation-related gene signatures for prognosis and immunity in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Previous studies indicate that lactylation, a post-translational modification, may play an important role in the progression of cervical cancer (CC). However, the comprehensive roles of lactylation in influencing the tumor microenvironment, immune landscape, and prognosis of CC have yet to be fully elucidated. The bulk RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq datasets of CC patients were downloaded from the Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus databases, respectively. A total of 630 genes associated with lactylation activity were identified using AUCell algorithm, differential expression, an
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
papers.summary: This study analyzed bulk and single-cell RNA-seq data from cervical cancer patients to identify lactylation-related gene signatures associated with prognosis and immune landscape. Using the AUCell algorithm and differential expression analysis, the authors identified 630 lactylation-associated genes and developed a prognostic signature linking lactylation to tumor microenvironment and immune infiltration. The findings suggest lactylation plays a role in cervical cancer progression and could inform prognostic stratification.

papers.title: Spatially resolved gene expression analysis illuminates location-specific functions in the reef-building coral Pocillopora acuta.
papers.abstract: Reef-building coral polyps contain multiple specialized tissue types with distinct functions, from feeding and defense to symbiosis and skeleton formation. While these cell types have been characterized microscopically and more recently via single-cell RNA sequencing, spatially resolved high-throughput gene expression profiling remains limited in corals. Here we combine Laser Capture Microdissection with RNA sequencing to characterize tissue-specific gene expression in the reef building coral Pocillopora acuta. Oral tissues, adjacent to the seawater, exhibited 1,253 upregulated genes enriched
papers.summary: This study uses laser capture microdissection combined with RNA sequencing to profile tissue-specific gene expression in the reef-building coral Pocillopora acuta. The authors identify over 1,200 genes upregulated in oral tissues near seawater, revealing location-specific functions that complement prior microscopic and single-cell RNA-seq characterizations. This provides a spatially resolved transcriptomic resource for understanding coral tissue specialization.

papers.title: Network-informed deconvolution of bulk immune gene co-expression reveals single-cell programs and spatial organization.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has opened unprecedented possibilities to explore the complexity of the immune system. However, existing methods primarily rely on expression-based clustering analysis, which lacks mechanistic explanations for immune cell states and encounters challenges in integrating multi-scale data.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a network-informed deconvolution approach that uses immune gene co-expression networks to extract single-cell programs from bulk RNA-seq data. This method links bulk expression to single-cell states and spatial organization, offering a mechanistic framework beyond standard expression-based clustering. It addresses challenges in integrating multi-scale immune data.

papers.title: Spatial compartmentalization of melanoma cell states reveals CAF-associated tumor cells with enhanced proliferative capacity.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are key components of the melanoma tumor microenvironment and have been implicated in immune evasion and therapy resistance. However, the spatial relationships between CAFs, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, and immune exclusion remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial profiling to map how cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) organize the melanoma tumor microenvironment, linking them to extracellular matrix remodeling and immune exclusion. The authors identify a distinct population of CAF-associated tumor cells with enhanced proliferative capacity, suggesting CAFs help create spatial niches that support tumor growth.

papers.title: Integrated Pan-Cancer, Single-Cell, and Spatial Transcriptomic Analyses Identify ZDHHC12 as a Biomarker Associated with Macrophage Infiltration and the Immune Landscape in Glioma.
papers.abstract: The tumor immune microenvironment (TME) critically influences cancer progression and therapeutic response. However, the pan-cancer expression landscape, prognostic relevance, and spatial distribution of ZDHHC12 remain incompletely characterized. This study investigated the prognostic value of ZDHHC12 and its associations with immune microenvironmental features and drug sensitivity.
papers.summary: This study integrates pan-cancer, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data to characterize the expression, prognostic value, and immune microenvironment associations of ZDHHC12, identifying it as a biomarker linked to macrophage infiltration in glioma. The findings suggest ZDHHC12 may influence the immune landscape and drug sensitivity, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target or prognostic marker.

papers.title: Shared genetic architecture of smoking dependence and Crohn's disease: A cross-trait analysis of GWAS summary statistics.
papers.abstract: Smoking dependence (SD) and Crohn's disease (CD) are epidemiologically associated, but whether this relationship reflects shared genetic susceptibility remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses cross-trait analysis of GWAS summary statistics to investigate whether smoking dependence and Crohn's disease share a genetic basis, beyond their known epidemiological association. The authors examine genetic overlap and potential shared risk loci between the two traits. The findings help clarify whether the comorbidity arises from common genetic susceptibility or from other factors.

papers.title: Spatial immune dysregulation in MASLD: integration of lobular zoning, metabolism and immune function.
papers.abstract: Most prior studies on immune-related fatty liver disease have focused on changes in immune cell quantity and composition. However, this "cell-count model" does not fully explain the regional onset of fibrosis, spatial heterogeneity of lesions, or variable immunotherapy responses. Immune dysregulation in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves not only compositional changes but also spatial redistribution and functional alterations of immune cells within specific hepatic lobule regions. Emerging multi-omics and spatial transcriptomic data suggest that chemokine
papers.summary: This review argues that immune dysregulation in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) cannot be explained by cell-count changes alone, but involves spatial redistribution and functional shifts of immune cells within specific hepatic lobule zones. It synthesizes emerging multi-omics and spatial transcriptomic evidence linking lobular zoning, metabolism, and immune function to explain regional fibrosis onset and variable immunotherapy responses.

papers.title: Spatial dynamics of cancer-associated fibroblasts links fibroblastic differentiation to immune exclusion and tumor progression.
papers.abstract: Although the role of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in cancer progression is increasingly recognized, their spatial dynamics and interactions with immune cells remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study examines how cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are spatially organized within tumors and how their differentiation states relate to immune cell exclusion and tumor progression. The authors link specific fibroblastic differentiation programs to the spatial exclusion of immune cells, suggesting CAFs actively shape the tumor immune microenvironment. These findings highlight spatial CAF heterogeneity as a driver of immune evasion.

papers.title: Case Report: Post-mortem analysis of long-term inflammation after mild COVID-19.
papers.abstract: Persistent inflammation and tissue injury may contribute to post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS). However, direct tissue evidence from mildly-infected individuals sampled long after recovery remains exceptionally limited. Here, we performed post-mortem bulk RNA-seq and GeoMx digital spatial profiling of lung, heart, and brain tissues from four individuals who recovered from mild COVID-19 more than 250 days before death from unrelated causes. Samples were collected during the early phase of the national vaccination program, before widespread vaccine uptake and recurrent infection, providing a ra
papers.summary: This case report performed post-mortem bulk RNA-seq and spatial profiling of lung, heart, and brain tissue from four people who had recovered from mild COVID-19 more than 250 days before dying of unrelated causes. The authors found evidence of persistent inflammation and tissue injury long after recovery, suggesting a possible tissue-level basis for post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS). The small sample size and case-report design limit generalization.
